summary: [RESOLVED 2026-08-25T06:32:52Z — root cause UNFIXED] CORRECTION + ESCALATION. Docker Desktop's Linux VM hard-failed at 2026-08-25T05:47:39Z with 'FATAL: running services: running fs: injecting event blocked for 60s' — dockerd stopped, hypervisor process stopped, ALL containers down. Every docker CLI call now returns 'Docker Desktop is unable to start'. This SUPERSEDES the root-cause attribution in dev-team-20260825T054306Z.json, which blamed an app-level blocked event loop in mcp-server. The mcp-server silence from 05:16:16Z was almost certainly the FIRST symptom of this same VM filesystem-sharing layer degrading, not an independent app bug. || UPDATE: outage lasted 45m13s and ended via a manual cold start from outside this session, NOT a self-heal and NOT the 06:00:41Z relaunch (which failed to bootstrap the engine). All 13 containers healthy, both named volumes intact, no data loss. Downgraded P0->P1: nothing is blocked now, but the fs event-injection FATAL is unaddressed and can re-wedge the VM at any time. See .payload.resolution.

payload.what_changed: That signal attributed the mcp-server wedge to an app-level event-loop block after a write-visibility error, with root cause UNCONFIRMED. Host-side Docker logs now show the failure is one layer down: the VM's filesystem event-injection service. The write-invisibility symptom (count=107, visible_now=0 at 05:16Z) is consistent with the fs-sharing layer failing to propagate writes, which is exactly the subsystem that later hard-blocked. Treat the mcp-server wedge as a DOWNSTREAM EFFECT, not the fault.

differential_diagnosis.NOT_hypervisor_crash: No ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/hypervisor.error.json exists, and /Users/admin/.docker/run/docker.sock IS present. This is NOT the 2026-07-15 signature (that one had the socket ABSENT plus a hypervisor.error.json virtualization error). Do NOT jump to that incident's exhausted recovery ladder.
differential_diagnosis.NOT_host_sleep: pmset -g log for 2026-08-25 shows no Sleep/Wake/DarkWake transitions across the incident window — only caffeinate assertions actively PREVENTING idle sleep. Host suspension is ruled out.
differential_diagnosis.NOT_process_restart: com.docker.backend (pid 14371) and Docker Desktop (pid 23968) both have lstart of 15 jul 2026 — the Docker Desktop processes have NOT restarted. The backend is alive (18.9% CPU) but its VM is gone.
differential_diagnosis.NOT_OOM: Last successful inspect of mcp-server-1 showed 508MiB/3GiB, RestartCount=0, CPU 0.18%.

asks: Diagnose the fs event-injection block — this is the virtiofs/osxfs file-sharing layer. Check which bind-mount was being watched when it blocked; the repo bind-mount (./docs/data, ./data/pdfs) is the prime suspect given the fleet writes those paths constantly.

[SATISFIED 06:32:52Z — daemon recovered via a manual cold start from outside this session. NOTE the original text below was WRONG and is retained only as a correction record: a normal restart was NOT sufficient — the 06:00:41Z relaunch failed to bootstrap the engine and a SECOND full launch was required.] Original: Recover the daemon. Because the socket exists and no hypervisor error was written, a normal Docker Desktop restart is the FIRST thing to try and is likely sufficient. Escalate to the user only if that fails.

CRITICAL SAFETY CONSTRAINT — do NOT under any circumstances 'rebuild the VM from scratch' (i.e. remove ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/Data/vms) as a recovery step. On Docker Desktop/Mac, named volumes live INSIDE the VM disk image; that step DESTROYED market_data and bctc-page-images on 2026-07-15 and required a 361MB backup restore. If the daemon does return, verify market_data volume integrity (row counts + MAX(date)) BEFORE trusting green health.

Investigate whether Docker Desktop's Resource Saver / pause feature is enabled. A pause->resume transition ~600ms before the fs FATAL suggests resume-from-pause is the trigger. If so, disabling Resource Saver is a candidate permanent fix for a recurring outage class.

[NOW TESTABLE — daemon is healthy as of 06:32:52Z] Re-check whether the mcp-server write-invisibility symptom (count=107, visible_now=0) still reproduces. If it does NOT, that confirms it was fs-layer collateral and the earlier app-level bug hypothesis (superseded signal dev-team-20260825T054306Z.json) can be formally closed.

RECURRENCE GUARD (new, promoted to primary ask now that the outage itself is over): the failure chain is reproducible-looking — pause->resume at 05:47:38.78Z, apiproxy broken-pipe burst, dockerd explicit Stop at 05:47:39.19Z, fs FATAL at 05:47:39.42Z. Capture Resource Saver / auto-pause settings state BEFORE changing anything, then treat ask 3 as the permanent fix candidate. Also worth noting: the first relaunch not bootstrapping means any runbook that says "just restart Docker Desktop" is insufficient — document the two-launch recovery.

probe_defect_found.what: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh mem_creep check misclassifies 'stats-unavailable' as a memory-threshold breach.
probe_defect_found.detail: This tick's verdict reports mem_creep FAIL with detail 'mem >= 85% threshold (A-30 WARN boundary, mem-creep gate)' listing all 10 containers as '(stats-unavailable)'. docker stats returning nothing because the daemon is DEAD is not memory creep — it is the absence of a reading. Reporting absence-of-data as a threshold breach is a false positive of exactly the class that erodes trust in the probe.
probe_defect_found.downstream_harm: The emitted signature is 'health_3000|mem_creep:<all 10 container names>'. That bogus 10-container signature is now written into docs/data/auditor-tier1-spawn-debounce.json (spawn_count=1, window_expires_at 2026-08-25T06:47:51Z). A genuine future single-container mem_creep will produce a DIFFERENT signature and will therefore not dedup against it — the debounce ledger has been polluted with an unrepeatable key.
probe_defect_found.fix: Treat stats-unavailable as a distinct third state (UNKNOWN/SKIP), never as FAIL. When the daemon itself is unreachable, mem_creep should be reported as not-evaluated and docker_ps should be the failing check.
probe_defect_found.scope_refinement: STILL VALID but narrower than first described. mem_creep only emits the false "mem >= 85% threshold" text in the TRANSIENT window where `docker ps -q` still lists containers but `docker stats` cannot read them. Once the daemon is fully unreachable (06:13:21Z tick) mem_creep degrades correctly, reporting "docker ps -q returned no output (docker unreachable?)". So the bug is a partial-daemon-failure path, not a total-outage path — which makes it harder to notice and worth fixing on its own merits.

second_probe_defect.what: docker_ps scored PASS in the same tick where the docker daemon is unreachable.
second_probe_defect.detail: The 05:47:51Z verdict records checks.docker_ps=PASS alongside health_3000=FAIL. Roughly 10 seconds later every docker CLI invocation returns 'Docker Desktop is unable to start'. Either docker_ps ran before the 05:47:50Z hypervisor stop (a genuine race, in which case it is merely stale), or its success predicate does not actually require a daemon response. Worth confirming which, because a docker_ps that can PASS with no daemon is a blind spot in the single most important check the probe has.
second_probe_defect.note: Timing makes the benign race plausible here — the probe wrote at 05:47:51Z and the hypervisor stopped at 05:47:50.55Z. Flagged for confirmation rather than asserted as a defect.
second_probe_defect.RESOLVED: CLOSED at 2026-08-25T06:13:21Z — this was the benign race, NOT a blind spot. It was filed as needs-confirmation rather than asserted, and the 06:13:21Z tick supplies the confirmation: with the daemon fully gone, docker_ps correctly returns FAIL with detail "docker ps returned no output (docker unreachable?)". The 05:47:51Z PASS was genuinely stale by ~1s against the 05:47:50.55Z hypervisor stop. No fix needed; ops should NOT spend time here.

third_probe_defect.what: Signature churn defeats spawn-debounce across a multi-phase outage.
third_probe_defect.evidence: docs/data/auditor-tier1-spawn-debounce.json now holds two entries for ONE incident, each spawn_count=1, neither suppressing the other: "health_3000|mem_creep:<10 container names>" (05:47:51Z) and "docker_ps|health_3000|health_3001|mem_creep" (06:13:21Z).
third_probe_defect.why: The signature is composed from the SET of currently-failing checks. A progressive infra failure changes that set at each phase, so every tick mints a fresh key and debounce never engages. Debounce only works for a failure that presents identically each time.
third_probe_defect.harm: Each T1 tick during a prolonged outage returns spawn_decision=SPAWN for what is one continuous incident. Absent a router-side judgement call, that is one subagent spawned per 30 minutes for the entire duration of the outage.
third_probe_defect.fix_direction: Debounce on incident identity rather than exact check-set equality — e.g. suppress when the new failing set is a SUPERSET of a still-in-window signature, or key on the most-severe failing check rather than the full concatenation.

resolution.how_it_recovered: NOT a self-heal. Backend log shows a FRESH COLD START at 06:32:51.230Z (desktop state:InitState + two pidfile "assuming pid re-use, removing it" warnings + feature-flag refetch + cli-context re-switch). This is a distinct, second launch — the 06:00:41Z relaunch reached onApplicationDidFinishLaunching but NEVER started the engine (no starting-engine line until 06:32:51.426Z). Router took no daemon action at any point (router-only scope); the second launch came from outside this session.

resolution.why_this_still_matters: The fs event-injection FATAL is UNFIXED. Recovery was a manual relaunch, not a repair. The same pause->resume transition can re-wedge the VM at any time, and the first relaunch attempt FAILING to bootstrap means recovery is not reliably one-click. Asks 0, 2, 3 below remain fully open.
